correctness.rationale: The Dirichlet ground-state transform with u_n=√n g_n gives conductance √(n(n+1)) and mass n, without an extra boundary edge. For λ↓0 and N=⌊λ^(-1/2)⌋ the resistance from a fixed site to N is log N+O(1). The resistance-linear test has energy 1/(log N+O(1)) and massive cost O((log N)^(-2)), using ∑_{n≤N} n(1+log(N/n))²=O(N²). Conversely, at that energy the mass on [N,2N] forces some |g_k|=O((log N)^(-1/2)); Cauchy–Schwarz along the path supplies the matching lower bound. In the finite-support variational quotient, small energy makes the g-values on the support differ by o(1), giving |g_m|²→1/S_V under unit defect normalization. Thus the reciprocal top Birman–Schwinger eigenvalue is asymptotic to 2/(S_V log(1/λ)); it increases continuously from zero to infinity. Finite-rank perturbation preserves the essential bottom zero, giving a negative isolated eigenvalue for every t>0. On the codimension-one hyperplane g_m=0 the defect is bounded by a fixed multiple of the gradient energy, so small t allows at most one negative eigenvalue counting multiplicity. Inverting the top-eigenvalue equation gives the claimed limit.
residual_risks: Fixed finite support and a nonnegative, nonzero V are required; the argument gives no multiplicative prefactor or strong-coupling eigenvalue count.

value.rationale: For the natural critical Hardy operator, qualitative instability leaves the eigenvalue scale undetermined. The exact logarithmic coefficient, depending only on the weighted defect mass across arbitrary fixed finite supports, distinguishes this case from algebraic weak binding and quantifies the instability; the one-state conclusion identifies the weak negative spectrum.
residual_risks: The coefficient does not quantify subexponential factors or predict uniformly moving defect supports.
